content.title: Structuring Test Classes for Maintainability
Mastering testng.xml: Flexible Test Suite Configuration
content.explanation:
**The Power of XML Configuration:**

testng.xml is the heart of TestNG's test suite configuration. It allows you to define which tests to run, how to run them, and with what parameters—all without changing your test code.

**Complete testng.xml Reference:**

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "http://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd">

<suite name="Complete Test Suite" 
       verbose="1" 
       parallel="tests" 
       thread-count="5"
       configfailurepolicy="continue"
       annotations="JDK"
       time-out="10000"
       skipfailedinvocationcounts="false"
       data-provider-thread-count="10"
       object-factory="com.example.CustomObjectFactory"
       allow-return-values="true">
    
    <!-- Suite-level parameters -->
    <parameter name="browser" value="chrome"/>
    <parameter name="environment" value="staging"/>
    <parameter name="base-url" value="https://staging.example.com"/>
    <parameter name="db-connection" value="jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/testdb"/>
    
    <!-- Listeners -->
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.CustomListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ReportListener"/>
        <listener class-name="org.testng.reporters.EmailableReporter2"/>
        <listener class-name="org.testng.reporters.XMLReporter"/>
    </listeners>
    
    <!-- Test definition 1: Smoke tests -->
    <test name="Smoke Tests" preserve-order="true">
        
        <!-- Test-level parameters (override suite) -->
        <parameter name="browser" value="firefox"/>
        <parameter name="smoke-specific" value="true"/>
        
        <!-- Group configuration -->
        <groups>
            <define name="all-smoke">
                <include name="smoke"/>
                <include name="critical"/>
            </define>
            
            <run>
                <include name="smoke"/>
                <exclude name="broken"/>
                <exclude name="flaky"/>
            </run>
            
            <dependencies>
                <group name="checkout" depends-on="login"/>
            </dependencies>
        </groups>
        
        <!-- Package to include all tests -->
        <packages>
            <package name="com.example.tests.smoke.*"/>
        </packages>
        
        <!-- Individual classes with method selection -->
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.LoginTest">
                <methods>
                    <include name="testValidLogin"/>
                    <include name="testRememberMe"/>
                    <exclude name=".*Invalid.*"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
            <class name="com.example.tests.SearchTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
    <!-- Test definition 2: Regression tests -->
    <test name="Regression Tests" parallel="classes" thread-count="4">
        <groups>
            <run>
                <include name="regression"/>
                <exclude name="broken"/>
            </run>
        </groups>
        
        <packages>
            <package name="com.example.tests.*"/>
        </packages>
    </test>
    
    <!-- Test definition 3: API tests with specific methods -->
    <test name="API Tests">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.api.UserApiTest">
                <methods>
                    <include name="testCreateUser"/>
                    <include name="testGetUser"/>
                    <include name="testUpdateUser"/>
                    <exclude name="testDeleteUser"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
            <class name="com.example.tests.api.ProductApiTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
    <!-- Test definition 4: Cross-browser tests -->
    <test name="Cross Browser Tests">
        <parameter name="browser" value="chrome"/>
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.ui.CrossBrowserTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
    <!-- Test definition 5: Data-driven tests with specific data provider -->
    <test name="Data-Driven Tests">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.DataDrivenTest">
                <methods>
                    <include name="testWithExternalData"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
</suite>
```

**Suite Element Attributes:**

| Attribute | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `name` | Suite name (appears in reports) | `name="My Test Suite"` |
| `verbose` | Logging level (0-10) | `verbose="2"` |
| `parallel` | Parallel execution mode | `parallel="tests"` |
| `thread-count` | Number of threads | `thread-count="5"` |
| `configfailurepolicy` | Behavior on config failure | `configfailurepolicy="continue"` |
| `time-out` | Default timeout (ms) | `time-out="10000"` |
| `skipfailedinvocationcounts` | Skip remaining invocations | `skipfailedinvocationcounts="false"` |
| `data-provider-thread-count` | Threads for data providers | `data-provider-thread-count="10"` |
| `allow-return-values` | Allow test methods to return values | `allow-return-values="true"` |

**Including and Excluding Tests:**

**By Package:**
```xml
<test name="Package Test">
    <packages>
        <package name="com.example.tests.*"/>
        <package name="com.example.tests.smoke.*"/>
        <package name="com.example.tests.regression.*"/>
    </packages>
</test>
```

**By Class:**
```xml
<test name="Class Test">
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.tests.LoginTest"/>
        <class name="com.example.tests.SearchTest"/>
        <class name="com.example.tests.CheckoutTest"/>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**By Method (include/exclude patterns):**
```xml
<test name="Method Test">
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.tests.UserTest">
            <methods>
                <!-- Include patterns (regex) -->
                <include name="test.*Valid.*"/>
                <include name=".*Success.*"/>
                
                <!-- Exclude patterns -->
                <exclude name=".*Invalid.*"/>
                <exclude name=".*Error.*"/>
                <exclude name="testSlowOperation"/>
                
                <!-- Specific methods in order (if preserve-order=true) -->
                <include name="testCreateUser"/>
                <include name="testLoginUser"/>
                <include name="testUpdateUser"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**By Group:**
```xml
<test name="Group Test">
    <groups>
        <!-- Define meta-groups -->
        <define name="all-critical">
            <include name="P0"/>
            <include name="P1"/>
        </define>
        
        <define name="smoke-and-critical">
            <include name="smoke"/>
            <include name="P0"/>
        </define>
        
        <!-- Which groups to run -->
        <run>
            <include name="smoke"/>
            <include name="regression"/>
            <exclude name="broken"/>
            <exclude name="flaky"/>
        </run>
        
        <!-- Group dependencies -->
        <dependencies>
            <group name="checkout" depends-on="login, cart"/>
            <group name="payment" depends-on="checkout"/>
        </dependencies>
    </groups>
    
    <packages>
        <package name="com.example.tests.*"/>
    </packages>
</test>
```

**Multi-Suite Configuration:**

You can create a master suite that includes other suite files:

```xml
<!-- master-suite.xml -->
<suite name="Master Suite">
    <suite-files>
        <suite-file path="smoke-tests.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="regression-tests.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="api-tests.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="ui-tests.xml"/>
    </suite-files>
</suite>
```

**Parameterized Suites:**

```xml
<!-- parameterized-suite.xml -->
<suite name="Parameterized Suite">
    <parameter name="browser" value="chrome"/>
    <parameter name="environment" value="staging"/>
    
    <test name="Test with Parameters">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.ParameterizedTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**Running testng.xml:**

**Command Line:**
```bash
java -cp testng.jar:build/classes org.testng.TestNG testng.xml
java -cp testng.jar:build/classes org.testng.TestNG suite1.xml suite2.xml
java -cp testng.jar:build/classes org.testng.TestNG -d test-output testng.xml
```

**Maven:**
```bash
mvn test -DsuiteXmlFile=testng.xml
mvn test -DsuiteXmlFile=smoke-tests.xml
mvn test -DsuiteXmlFile=src/test/resources/testng.xml
```

**Gradle:**
```bash
./gradlew test -Dtestng.suite.file=testng.xml
./gradlew test -Psuite=smoke-tests.xml
```

**IntelliJ:** Right-click on testng.xml → Run '...'

**Eclipse:** Right-click on testng.xml → Run As → TestNG Suite

steps.action: Create a testng.xml file that defines your base configuration.
details: Create `testng.xml` in your project root:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "http://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd">

<suite name="E-Commerce Test Suite" verbose="1">
    
    <!-- Global parameters -->
    <parameter name="environment" value="staging"/>
    <parameter name="browser" value="chrome"/>
    <parameter name="headless" value="true"/>
    
    <!-- Listeners for reporting -->
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ExtentReportListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.SlackNotifier"/>

    <!-- Include all test files -->
    <suite-files>
        <suite-file path="testng-smoke.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="testng-regression.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="testng-api.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="testng-ui.xml"/>
    </suite-files>
    
</suite>
```

steps.action: Configure build tools to use the test suites.
details:
**Maven `pom.xml` configuration:**
```xml
<profiles>
    <profile>
        <id>smoke-tests</id>
        <build>
            <plugins>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                    <configuration>
                        <suiteXmlFiles>
                            <suiteXmlFile>testng-smoke.xml</suiteXmlFile>
                        </suiteXmlFiles>
                    </configuration>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </build>
    </profile>
    
    <profile>
        <id>regression-tests</id>
        <build>
            <plugins>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                    <configuration>
                        <suiteXmlFiles>
                            <suiteXmlFile>testng-regression.xml</suiteXmlFile>
                        </suiteXmlFiles>
                    </configuration>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </build>
    </profile>
</profiles>
```

**Jenkins Pipeline:**
```groovy
pipeline {
    stages {
        stage('Smoke Tests') {
            steps {
                sh 'mvn test -Psmoke-tests -Denvironment=staging'
            }
        }
        stage('Regression Tests') {
            when { branch 'main' }
            steps {
                sh 'mvn test -Pregression-tests -Denvironment=staging'
            }
        }
        stage('Production Smoke') {
            when { tag 'release-*' }
            steps {
                sh 'mvn test -Psmoke-tests -Denvironment=production'
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**GitHub Actions:**
```yaml
name: Test Suite
on: [push]

jobs:
  smoke-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run Smoke Tests
        run: mvn test -Psmoke-tests -Denvironment=staging
  
  regression-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run Regression Tests
        run: mvn test -Pregression-tests -Denvironment=staging
```
steps.verification: CI/CD pipeline can run different test suites with appropriate parameters.

steps.action: Execute the test suites and verify they run correctly.
details:
```bash
# Run smoke tests
mvn test -Psmoke-tests

# Run regression tests
mvn test -Pregression-tests

# Run API tests only
mvn test -DsuiteXmlFile=testng-api.xml

# Run with specific environment
mvn test -Psmoke-tests -Denvironment=production

# Run master suite
mvn test -DsuiteXmlFile=testng.xml
```

After running, check the test reports in `target/surefire-reports/index.html` to ensure all tests executed correctly.

content.title: The Complete testng.xml Reference
content.explanation:
**Understanding the XML Configuration File:**

testng.xml is the central configuration file for TestNG test suites. It allows you to define which tests to run, how to run them, and with what parameters—all without modifying your test code.

**Basic XML Structure:**

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "http://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd">

<suite name="My Test Suite">
    <test name="My Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.MyTestClass"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**Document Type Definition (DTD):**

The DOCTYPE declaration points to the TestNG DTD, which defines the valid structure of the XML file. This enables validation in IDEs.

**Hierarchical Structure:**

```
<suite> (top-level, represents one test suite)
    ├── <parameters> (suite-level parameters)
    ├── <listeners> (suite-level listeners)
    ├── <packages> (package-level test inclusion)
    ├── <test> (represents one test run)
    │   ├── <parameters> (test-level parameters)
    │   ├── <groups> (group configuration)
    │   ├── <packages> (packages to include)
    │   └── <classes> (classes to include)
    │       └── <class> (individual test class)
    │           └── <methods> (method-level selection)
    │               ├── <include> (include specific methods)
    │               └── <exclude> (exclude specific methods)
    └── <suite-files> (include other suite files)
```

**Complete Example with All Elements:**

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "http://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd">

<suite name="Complete Test Suite" 
       verbose="2" 
       parallel="tests" 
       thread-count="5"
       configfailurepolicy="continue"
       annotations="JDK"
       time-out="10000"
       skipfailedinvocationcounts="false"
       data-provider-thread-count="10"
       object-factory="com.example.CustomObjectFactory"
       allow-return-values="true"
       preserve-order="true"
       group-by-instances="false">

    <!-- Suite-level parameters (available to all tests) -->
    <parameter name="environment" value="staging"/>
    <parameter name="browser" value="chrome"/>
    <parameter name="base-url" value="https://staging.example.com"/>

    <!-- Suite-level listeners -->
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.CustomListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ExtentReportListener"/>
        <listener class-name="org.testng.reporters.EmailableReporter2"/>
        <listener class-name="org.testng.reporters.XMLReporter"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.RetryListener"/>
    </listeners>

    <!-- First test: Smoke tests -->
    <test name="Smoke Tests" preserve-order="true">
        <!-- Test-level parameters (override suite) -->
        <parameter name="browser" value="firefox"/>
        <parameter name="headless" value="true"/>

        <!-- Group configuration -->
        <groups>
            <define name="smoke-with-critical">
                <include name="smoke"/>
                <include name="critical"/>
            </define>

            <run>
                <include name="smoke"/>
                <include name="critical"/>
                <exclude name="broken"/>
                <exclude name="flaky"/>
            </run>

            <dependencies>
                <group name="checkout" depends-on="login, cart"/>
            </dependencies>
        </groups>

        <!-- Packages to include -->
        <packages>
            <package name="com.example.tests.smoke.*"/>
            <package name="com.example.tests.login.*"/>
        </packages>

        <!-- Individual classes with method selection -->
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.LoginTest">
                <methods>
                    <include name="testValidLogin"/>
                    <include name="testRememberMe"/>
                    <exclude name=".*Invalid.*"/>
                    <exclude name="testSlowOperation"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
            <class name="com.example.tests.SearchTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>

    <!-- Second test: Regression tests -->
    <test name="Regression Tests" parallel="classes" thread-count="4">
        <groups>
            <run>
                <include name="regression"/>
                <exclude name="broken"/>
            </run>
        </groups>
        <packages>
            <package name="com.example.tests.*"/>
        </packages>
    </test>

    <!-- Third test: API tests with method selection -->
    <test name="API Tests">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.api.UserApiTest">
                <methods>
                    <include name="testCreateUser"/>
                    <include name="testGetUser"/>
                    <include name="testUpdateUser"/>
                    <exclude name="testDeleteUser"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
            <class name="com.example.tests.api.ProductApiTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>

    <!-- Fourth test: Parameterized tests -->
    <test name="Parameterized Tests">
        <parameter name="data-source" value="excel"/>
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.DataDrivenTest">
                <methods>
                    <include name="testWithExternalData"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
        </classes>
    </test>

    <!-- Include external suite files -->
    <suite-files>
        <suite-file path="testng-chrome.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="testng-firefox.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="testng-edge.xml"/>
    </suite-files>

</suite>
```

**Suite Element Attributes:**

| Attribute | Description | Example | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|---------|
| `name` | Suite name (appears in reports) | `name="My Suite"` | Required |
| `verbose` | Logging level (0-10) | `verbose="2"` | 1 |
| `parallel` | Parallel execution mode | `parallel="tests"` | none |
| `thread-count` | Number of threads | `thread-count="5"` | 5 |
| `configfailurepolicy` | Behavior on config failure | `configfailurepolicy="continue"` | `skip` |
| `time-out` | Default timeout (ms) | `time-out="10000"` | none |
| `skipfailedinvocationcounts` | Skip remaining invocations | `skipfailedinvocationcounts="true"` | false |
| `data-provider-thread-count` | Threads for data providers | `data-provider-thread-count="10"` | 10 |
| `object-factory` | Custom object factory class | `object-factory="com.example.Factory"` | none |
| `allow-return-values` | Allow test methods to return values | `allow-return-values="true"` | false |
| `preserve-order` | Preserve method order | `preserve-order="true"` | true |
| `group-by-instances` | Group tests by instance | `group-by-instances="false"` | false |
| `junit` | Run JUnit tests | `junit="true"` | false |
| `mixed` | Mix TestNG and JUnit | `mixed="true"` | false |

**Test Element Attributes:**

| Attribute | Description | Example | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|---------|
| `name` | Test name (appears in reports) | `name="Smoke Tests"` | Required |
| `enabled` | Enable/disable this test | `enabled="true"` | true |
| `preserve-order` | Preserve method order | `preserve-order="true"` | true |
| `parallel` | Parallel mode for this test | `parallel="methods"` | none |
| `thread-count` | Threads for this test | `thread-count="3"` | from suite |
| `time-out` | Timeout for this test | `time-out="5000"` | none |
| `junit` | Run as JUnit | `junit="false"` | false |
| `skipfailedinvocationcounts` | Skip failed invocations | `skipfailedinvocationcounts="false"` | false |

**Including and Excluding Tests:**

**By Package:**
```xml
<test name="Package Test">
    <packages>
        <!-- Include all tests in a package -->
        <package name="com.example.tests.*"/>
        
        <!-- Include specific package -->
        <package name="com.example.tests.smoke"/>
        
        <!-- Exclude a package -->
        <package name="com.example.tests.legacy"
                 excluded-patterns="com.example.tests.legacy.*"/>
    </packages>
</test>
```

**By Class:**
```xml
<test name="Class Test">
    <classes>
        <!-- Single class -->
        <class name="com.example.tests.LoginTest"/>
        
        <!-- Multiple classes -->
        <class name="com.example.tests.SearchTest"/>
        <class name="com.example.tests.CheckoutTest"/>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**By Method (with patterns):**
```xml
<test name="Method Test">
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.tests.UserTest">
            <methods>
                <!-- Include patterns (regex) -->
                <include name="test.*Valid.*"/>
                <include name=".*Success.*"/>
                
                <!-- Exclude patterns -->
                <exclude name=".*Invalid.*"/>
                <exclude name=".*Error.*"/>
                <exclude name="testSlowOperation"/>
                
                <!-- Specific methods in order (if preserve-order=true) -->
                <include name="testCreateUser"/>
                <include name="testLoginUser"/>
                <include name="testUpdateUser"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**Including/Excluding by Annotation:**

You can also use annotations in test classes to control execution.

```java
@Test(groups = {"smoke", "regression"})
public class SmokeTest {
    
    @Test(groups = {"critical"})
    public void testCritical() { }
    
    @Test(enabled = false)
    public void testDisabled() { }
}
```

**XML Validation:**

Most IDEs validate testng.xml against the DTD. Common validation errors:

| Error | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `cvc-complex-type.2.4.a` | Invalid element order | Ensure elements are in correct order (groups before classes) |
| `cvc-attribute.3` | Invalid attribute value | Check attribute values (e.g., parallel values) |
| `cvc-pattern-valid` | Invalid regex pattern | Fix regex syntax in include/exclude patterns |
| Element type must be declared | Missing DOCTYPE | Add `<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM ...>` |

steps.action: Plan the organization of your test suites.
details: For a typical enterprise application, you might have:

```
test-suites/
├── master-suite.xml              # Master configuration
├── smoke/
│   ├── smoke-suite.xml           # Critical path tests
│   └── smoke-chrome.xml           # Browser-specific smoke
├── regression/
│   ├── regression-suite.xml       # Full regression
│   ├── regression-api.xml         # API regression
│   └── regression-ui.xml          # UI regression
├── integration/
│   ├── integration-db.xml         # Database tests
│   └── integration-services.xml    # Service integration
├── performance/
│   ├── performance-load.xml       # Load tests
│   └── performance-stress.xml     # Stress tests
└── environments/
```

content.title: Mastering Test Groups in testng.xml
content.explanation:
**Groups: The Ultimate Test Organization Tool**

Groups allow you to categorize tests and run them selectively. testng.xml provides powerful group configuration options.

**Defining Groups in Test Classes:**

```java
public class GroupExamples {
    
    @Test(groups = {"smoke", "login"})
    public void testValidLogin() { }
    
    @Test(groups = {"smoke", "login", "critical"})
    public void testLoginWithRememberMe() { }
    
    @Test(groups = {"regression", "login"})
    public void testInvalidLogin() { }
    
    @Test(groups = {"database", "slow"})
    public void testDatabaseQuery() { }
    
    @Test(groups = {"api", "user-service"})
    public void testGetUser() { }
    
    @Test(groups = {"api", "order-service"})
    public void testCreateOrder() { }
}
```

**Basic Group Inclusion/Exclusion:**

```xml
<test name="Group Test">
    <groups>
        <run>
            <!-- Include these groups -->
            <include name="smoke"/>
            <include name="critical"/>
            
            <!-- Exclude these groups -->
            <exclude name="broken"/>
            <exclude name="flaky"/>
            <exclude name="slow"/>
        </run>
    </groups>
    
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.GroupExamples"/>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**Defining Meta-Groups:**

```xml
<test name="Meta-Group Test">
    <groups>
        <!-- Define meta-groups -->
        <define name="all-smoke">
            <include name="smoke"/>
            <include name="critical"/>
        </define>
        
        <define name="quick-tests">
            <include name="smoke"/>
            <include name="unit"/>
            <exclude name="slow"/>
        </define>
        
        <define name="full-regression">
            <include name="regression"/>
            <include name="integration"/>
            <include name="database"/>
        </define>
        
        <!-- Run using meta-groups -->
        <run>
            <include name="all-smoke"/>
            <include name="quick-tests"/>
            <exclude name="full-regression"/>
        </run>
    </groups>
    
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.GroupExamples"/>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**Group Dependencies:**

```xml
<test name="Group Dependencies">
    <groups>
        <dependencies>
            <!-- These groups depend on others -->
            <group name="checkout" depends-on="login, cart"/>
            <group name="payment" depends-on="checkout"/>
            <group name="order-confirmation" depends-on="payment"/>
            <group name="full-e2e" depends-on="login, checkout, payment, order"/>
        </dependencies>
        
        <run>
            <include name="full-e2e"/>
        </run>
    </groups>
    
    <packages>
        <package name="com.example.tests.e2e.*"/>
    </packages>
</test>
```

**Group-Based Test Selection Examples:**

| Scenario | XML Configuration |
|----------|-------------------|
| Run only smoke tests | `<include name="smoke"/>` |
| Run all except broken | `<exclude name="broken"/>` |
| Run critical tests in production | `<include name="critical"/>` |
| Run API tests only | `<include name="api"/>` |
| Run quick tests (no slow ones) | `<exclude name="slow"/>` |
| Run tests that modify data | `<include name="data-modifying"/>` |
| Run read-only tests | `<include name="read-only"/>` |

**Advanced Group Configuration:**

```xml
<test name="Advanced Group Test">
    <groups>
        <!-- Meta-group definitions -->
        <define name="critical-path">
            <include name="smoke"/>
            <include name="login"/>
            <include name="checkout"/>
            <include name="payment"/>
        </define>
        
        <define name="data-verification">
            <include name="database"/>
            <include name="consistency"/>
            <include name="integrity"/>
        </define>
        
        <define name="performance-sensitive">
            <include name="performance"/>
            <include name="load"/>
            <exclude name="slow"/>
        </define>
        
        <!-- Complex dependencies -->
        <dependencies>
            <group name="checkout" depends-on="login, cart"/>
            <group name="payment" depends-on="checkout"/>
            <group name="inventory" depends-on="product-catalog"/>
            <group name="order-fulfillment" depends-on="payment, inventory"/>
        </dependencies>
        
        <!-- Run configuration -->
        <run>
            <!-- Include multiple meta-groups -->
            <include name="critical-path"/>
            <include name="performance-sensitive"/>
            
            <!-- Exclude specific groups -->
            <exclude name="broken"/>
            <exclude name="wip"/>
            <exclude name="experimental"/>
        </run>
    </groups>
    
    <!-- Multiple packages -->
    <packages>
        <package name="com.example.tests.business.*"/>
        <package name="com.example.tests.services.*"/>
        <package name="com.example.tests.data.*"/>
    </packages>
    
    <!-- Additional classes with method selection -->
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.tests.special.MigrationTest">
            <methods>
                <include name="test.*Data.*"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**Running Groups from Command Line:**

```bash
# Run specific groups
java -cp testng.jar:build/classes org.testng.TestNG -groups smoke,regression testng.xml

# Exclude groups
java -cp testng.jar:build/classes org.testng.TestNG -excludegroups broken,flaky testng.xml

# Run groups with patterns
java -cp testng.jar:build/classes org.testng.TestNG -groups "smoke|critical" testng.xml
```

**Maven Integration:**

```xml
<!-- pom.xml -->
<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
            <configuration>
                <groups>smoke,regression</groups>
                <excludedGroups>broken,flaky</excludedGroups>
            </configuration>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>
```

**Gradle Integration:**

```groovy
test {
    useTestNG() {
        includeGroups 'smoke', 'regression'
        excludeGroups 'broken', 'flaky'
    }
}
```

**Group-Based Reporting:**

TestNG reports include statistics by group, showing:
- Total tests per group
- Pass/fail counts per group
- Execution time per group
- Success rate by group

**Best Practices for Groups:**

| Practice | Example | Benefit |
|----------|---------|---------|
| Use consistent naming | `smoke`, `regression`, `api` | Easy to remember |
| Document group meanings | Javadoc on test classes | Clear purpose |
| Use meta-groups for common combinations | `critical-path` | Reduce duplication |
| Mark flaky tests | `flaky` group | Easy to exclude in CI |
| Environment-specific groups | `dev-only`, `prod-safe` | Prevent destructive tests in prod |
| Priority groups | `P0`, `P1`, `P2` | Prioritize test execution |

content.title: Controlling Test Execution Order with Priorities
content.explanation:
**Priorities: When Order Matters**

Test priorities determine the order in which test methods execute. Lower priority numbers run first.

**Priority Basics:**

```java
public class PriorityTest {
    
    @Test(priority = 1)
    public void testCreateUser() {
        System.out.println("1. Create user");
    }
    
    @Test(priority = 2)
    public void testLoginUser() {
        System.out.println("2. Login user");
    }
    
    @Test(priority = 3)
    public void testUpdateUser() {
        System.out.println("3. Update user");
    }
    
    @Test(priority = 4)
    public void testDeleteUser() {
        System.out.println("4. Delete user");
    }
    
    @Test // No priority = default 0
    public void testDefaultPriority() {
        System.out.println("0. Default priority");
    }
}
```

**Setting Priorities in testng.xml:**

```xml
<test name="Priority Test">
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.PriorityTest">
            <methods>
                <!-- Priority can be set in XML too -->
                <include name="testCreateUser" priority="1"/>
                <include name="testLoginUser" priority="2"/>
                <include name="testUpdateUser" priority="3"/>
                <include name="testDeleteUser" priority="4"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**Priority with preserve-order:**

```xml
<!-- preserve-order="true" respects XML order first, then priority -->
<test name="Mixed Order" preserve-order="true">
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.PriorityTest">
            <methods>
                <!-- These will run in XML order first -->
                <include name="testLoginUser" priority="2"/>
                <include name="testCreateUser" priority="1"/>
                <include name="testDeleteUser" priority="4"/>
                <include name="testUpdateUser" priority="3"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**Priority with Dependencies:**

```java
public class PriorityWithDependenciesTest {
    
    @Test(priority = 1)
    public void testSetup() {
        System.out.println("Setup - runs first");
    }
    
    // dependsOnMethods overrides priority
    @Test(priority = 3, dependsOnMethods = {"testSetup"})
    public void testMain() {
        System.out.println("Main - runs after setup despite higher priority");
    }
    
    @Test(priority = 2, dependsOnMethods = {"testMain"})
    public void testCleanup() {
        System.out.println("Cleanup - runs after main despite lower priority");
    }
}
```

**Priority Strategies:**

| Strategy | Priority Range | Use Case |
|----------|----------------|----------|
| **Critical Path** | 1-10 | Tests that must run first |
| **Core Features** | 11-50 | Main functionality tests |
| **Edge Cases** | 51-100 | Boundary condition tests |
| **Cleanup** | 1000+ | Tests that should run last |

**Example: Complete Priority Strategy**

```xml
<test name="E-Commerce Test Suite with Priorities">
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.tests.SetupTest">
            <methods>
                <include name="testDatabaseConnection" priority="1"/>
                <include name="testLoadTestData" priority="2"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
        
        <class name="com.example.tests.LoginTest">
            <methods>
                <include name="testValidLogin" priority="10"/>
                <include name="testRememberMe" priority="11"/>
                <include name="testInvalidLogin" priority="50"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
        
        <class name="com.example.tests.CheckoutTest">
            <methods>
                <include name="testAddToCart" priority="20"/>
                <include name="testCheckoutProcess" priority="21"/>
                <include name="testPayment" priority="22"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
        
        <class name="com.example.tests.CleanupTest">
            <methods>
                <include name="testCleanupData" priority="1000"/>
                <include name="testCloseConnections" priority="1001"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**Priority Best Practices:**

1. **Use priorities for logical order, not dependencies**
2. **Combine priorities with `preserve-order="true"` for predictable execution**
3. **Document priority ranges** in team guidelines
4. **Use dependencies for mandatory prerequisites**
5. **Avoid negative priorities** (can be confusing)
6. **Leave gaps** (1,10,20) for future insertions
7. **Consider parallel execution** - priorities may not guarantee order in parallel mode

content.title: Conditional Test Execution in testng.xml
Advanced testng.xml Features
content.explanation:
**Going Beyond the Basics:**

testng.xml offers many advanced features for complex test scenarios.

**1. Custom Listeners**

Listeners allow you to hook into the test lifecycle.

```xml
<suite name="Listener Demo">
    <listeners>
        <!-- Multiple listeners in order -->
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.LoggingListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ScreenshotListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.RetryListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.SlackNotifier"/>
        
        <!-- Parameterized listeners -->
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.EmailListener">
            <parameter name="recipients" value="qa@example.com"/>
            <parameter name="smtp-server" value="smtp.company.com"/>
        </listener>
    </listeners>
    
    <test name="Listener Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.ListenerTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**2. Method Interceptors**

Method interceptors can dynamically change test execution order.

```xml
<suite name="Interceptor Demo">
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.interceptors.PriorityInterceptor"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.interceptors.FlakyTestInterceptor"/>
    </listeners>
    
    <test name="Interceptor Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.InterceptorTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**3. Custom Method Selectors**

Method selectors provide fine-grained control over which tests run.

```xml
<test name="Selector Demo">
    <method-selectors>
        <!-- Multiple selectors (AND condition) -->
        <method-selector>
            <selector-class name="com.example.selectors.TimeBasedSelector"/>
        </method-selector>
        
        <method-selector>
            <selector-class name="com.example.selectors.ResourceBasedSelector"/>
        </method-selector>
        
        <!-- BeanShell selector with priority -->
        <method-selector priority="1">
            <script language="beanshell">
                <![CDATA[
                    // Custom selection logic
                    return testngMethod.getMethodName().startsWith("test");
                ]]>
            </script>
        </method-selector>
    </method-selectors>
    
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.SelectorTest"/>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**4. Object Factories**

Object factories control how test classes are instantiated.

```xml
<suite name="Factory Demo" object-factory="com.example.factories.CustomObjectFactory">
    <parameter name="injection-mode" value="guice"/>
    
    <test name="Factory Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.FactoryTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**5. Dependency Injection**

TestNG supports Guice for dependency injection.

```xml
<suite name="Guice Demo">
    <test name="Guice Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.GuiceTest">
                <methods>
                    <!-- Methods can receive injected parameters -->
                    <include name="testWithInjection"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**6. YAML Configuration**

TestNG also supports YAML format for suite configuration.

```yaml
# testng.yaml
name: YAML Suite
verbose: 2
parallel: tests
threadCount: 5
parameters:
  - name: browser
    value: chrome
  - name: environment
    value: staging
listeners:
  - com.example.listeners.CustomListener
tests:
  - name: Smoke Tests
    groups:
      run:
        - smoke
        - critical
    packages:
      - com.example.tests.smoke.*
  - name: Regression Tests
    groups:
      run:
        - regression
    packages:
      - com.example.tests.*
```

**7. Annotation Transformers**

Annotation transformers can modify annotations at runtime.

```xml
<suite name="Transformer Demo">
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.transformers.AnnotationTransformer"/>
    </listeners>
    
    <test name="Transformer Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.TransformerTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**8. Retry Analyzers**

Retry failed tests automatically.

```xml
<suite name="Retry Demo">
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.retry.RetryListener"/>
    </listeners>
    
    <test name="Retry Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.RetryTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**9. Parallel Execution Strategies**

```xml
<suite name="Parallel Demo" parallel="tests" thread-count="5">
    
    <!-- Methods within a class in parallel -->
    <test name="Method Parallel" parallel="methods" thread-count="3">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.MethodParallelTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
    <!-- Classes in parallel -->
    <test name="Class Parallel" parallel="classes" thread-count="2">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.ClassParallelTest1"/>
            <class name="com.example.ClassParallelTest2"/>
            <class name="com.example.ClassParallelTest3"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
    <!-- Instances in parallel -->
    <test name="Instance Parallel" parallel="instances" thread-count="4">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.InstanceParallelTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
</suite>
```

**10. Data Provider Thread Configuration**

```xml
<suite name="DataProvider Demo" data-provider-thread-count="10">
    <test name="DataProvider Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.DataProviderTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**11. Timeout Configuration**

```xml
<suite name="Timeout Demo" time-out="30000">
    <test name="Timeout Test" time-out="10000">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.TimeoutTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**12. Configuration Failure Policy**

```xml
<suite name="Config Failure Demo" configfailurepolicy="continue">
    <!-- continue: run tests even if config fails -->
    <!-- skip: skip tests if config fails -->
    
    <test name="Config Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.ConfigFailureTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**13. Preserve Order vs. Priority**

```xml
<test name="Order Test" preserve-order="true">
    <!-- preserve-order respects XML order -->
    <!-- priority still works within that order -->
    <classes>
        <class name="com.example.OrderTest">
            <methods>
                <include name="testB" priority="2"/>
                <include name="testA" priority="1"/>
                <include name="testC" priority="3"/>
            </methods>
        </class>
    </classes>
</test>
```

**14. Mixed Mode (TestNG + JUnit)**

```xml
<suite name="Mixed Mode" mixed="true">
    <test name="JUnit Tests" junit="true">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.JUnitTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
    <test name="TestNG Tests">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.TestNGTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**15. Complete Advanced Example**

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "http://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd">

<suite name="Advanced Test Suite" 
       verbose="2" 
       parallel="tests" 
       thread-count="5"
       configfailurepolicy="continue"
       data-provider-thread-count="10"
       object-factory="com.example.factories.CustomFactory"
       allow-return-values="true">
    
    <!-- Global parameters -->
    <parameter name="global-config" value="config.properties"/>
    
    <!-- Listeners -->
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ExecutionListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.AnnotationTransformer"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.retry.RetryAnalyzerListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.reporting.ExtentReportListener"/>
    </listeners>
    
    <!-- Method interceptors -->
    <method-selectors>
        <method-selector>
            <selector-class name="com.example.selectors.PriorityBasedSelector"/>
        </method-selector>
    </method-selectors>
    
    <!-- Test with all advanced features -->
    <test name="Advanced Features Test" parallel="methods" thread-count="3">
        <parameter name="test-level" value="advanced"/>
        
        <groups>
            <define name="all-critical">
                <include name="P0"/>
                <include name="P1"/>
            </define>
            <run>
                <include name="all-critical"/>
                <exclude name="broken"/>
            </run>
            <dependencies>
                <group name="checkout" depends-on="login"/>
            </dependencies>
        </groups>
        
        <packages>
            <package name="com.example.tests.advanced.*"/>
        </packages>
        
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.tests.SpecialTest">
                <methods>
                    <include name="testSpecial"/>
                </methods>
            </class>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
    <!-- Include external suites -->
    <suite-files>
        <suite-file path="testng-smoke.xml"/>
        <suite-file path="testng-regression.xml"/>
    </suite-files>
    
</suite>
```

**Summary: Advanced Features Cheat Sheet**

| Feature | XML Element/Attribute | Purpose |
|---------|----------------------|---------|
| Listeners | `<listeners>` | Hook into test lifecycle |
| Method Selectors | `<method-selectors>` | Dynamic test selection |
| Object Factory | `object-factory` | Custom instantiation |
| Interceptors | `<listeners>` with custom class | Modify test behavior |
| Retry Analyzer | `<listeners>` | Auto-retry failed tests |
| Annotation Transformer | `<listeners>` | Modify annotations at runtime |
| Mixed Mode | `mixed="true"` | Run JUnit and TestNG together |
| Data Provider Threads | `data-provider-thread-count` | Parallel data-driven tests |
| Config Failure Policy | `configfailurepolicy` | Behavior on setup failure |
| Preserve Order | `preserve-order` | Respect XML method order |
| Group Dependencies | `<dependencies>` | Test execution dependencies |
| Meta-Groups | `<define>` | Group combinations |
| BeanShell | `<script>` | Complex conditions |

content.title: Why Parallel Execution? The Performance Imperative
content.explanation:
**The Need for Speed:**

As test suites grow, execution time becomes a critical bottleneck. A suite that takes an hour to run sequentially can be reduced to minutes with proper parallelization.

**The Problem with Sequential Execution:**

```
Test Suite: 1000 tests × 5 seconds each = 5000 seconds (83 minutes)

Sequential execution: 1 hour 23 minutes
Parallel (10 threads): ~8 minutes
Parallel (50 threads): ~2 minutes
```

**Parallel Execution Modes in TestNG:**

TestNG supports four levels of parallel execution, each with different characteristics and use cases.

| Mode | Description | Best For | Example |
|------|-------------|----------|---------|
| **methods** | Run test methods in separate threads | Independent unit tests | `<suite parallel="methods" thread-count="10">` |
| **tests** | Run `<test>` tags in separate threads | Different test suites | `<suite parallel="tests" thread-count="5">` |
| **classes** | Run test classes in separate threads | Classes with independent tests | `<suite parallel="classes" thread-count="8">` |
| **instances** | Run instances in separate threads | Data-driven tests | `<suite parallel="instances" thread-count="4">` |

**How Parallel Execution Works:**

TestNG creates a thread pool and assigns tests to available threads based on the configured mode.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│         TestNG Thread Pool          │
│  ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐  │
│  │Thread 1│ │Thread 2│ │Thread 3│  │
│  └────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘  │
└───────────┬────────────┬───────────┘
            │             │
    ┌───────▼───────┐ ┌───▼────────┐
    │  Test Class A │ │ Test Class B│
    │  - test1()    │ │ - test3()   │
    │  - test2()    │ │ - test4()   │
    └───────────────┘ └────────────┘
```

**Parallel vs. Sequential: Performance Comparison**

| Test Count | Sequential | Parallel (10 threads) | Parallel (50 threads) |
|------------|------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 100 tests | 500 seconds | 50 seconds | 10 seconds |
| 500 tests | 2500 seconds | 250 seconds | 50 seconds |
| 1000 tests | 5000 seconds | 500 seconds | 100 seconds |
| 5000 tests | 25000 seconds | 2500 seconds | 500 seconds |

**When to Use Parallel Execution:**

✅ **Good Candidates:**
- Independent unit tests
- API tests (no shared state)
- Read-only database tests
- Stateless service tests

❌ **Poor Candidates:**
- Tests that share global state
- Tests that modify shared data
- Tests that use limited resources (single database connection)
- UI tests sharing the same browser instance

**Key Challenges:**

| Challenge | Description | Solution |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| **Thread Safety** | Tests interfere with each other | Use ThreadLocal, avoid static state |
| **Resource Contention** | Limited CPU, memory, connections | Monitor resources, cap thread count |
| **Data Isolation** | Tests modify shared test data | Unique data per thread, database transactions |
| **Debugging** | Harder to debug parallel failures | Thread-safe logging, thread IDs in logs |
| **Reporting** | Reports need thread context | TestNG handles automatically |

questions.question: What are the different ways to configure listeners in TestNG?
questions.answer:
**Multiple Configuration Options:**

TestNG provides several flexible ways to attach listeners to your tests.

**1. testng.xml Configuration (Most Common)**

```xml
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "http://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd">

<suite name="Listener Demo Suite">
    
    <!-- Suite-level listeners -->
    <listeners>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.TestExecutionListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.SuiteExecutionListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ScreenshotListener"/>
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.PerformanceListener"/>
        
        <!-- Parameterized listener -->
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.EmailListener">
            <parameter name="recipients" value="qa@example.com"/>
            <parameter name="smtp-server" value="smtp.company.com"/>
        </listener>
    </listeners>
    
    <test name="Listener Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.ListenerTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
    
</suite>
```

**2. @Listeners Annotation**

```java
import org.testng.annotations.Listeners;

// Class-level listeners
@Listeners({
    com.example.listeners.TestExecutionListener.class,
    com.example.listeners.ScreenshotListener.class,
    com.example.listeners.PerformanceListener.class
})
public class AnnotatedListenerTest {
    
    @Test
    public void testWithListeners() {
        System.out.println("Test with class-level listeners");
    }
}

// Method-specific listeners (not directly supported, but can be achieved with custom logic)
```

**3. Service Loader (Java's SPI)**

Create `META-INF/services/org.testng.ITestNGListener` file:
```
com.example.listeners.TestExecutionListener
com.example.listeners.SuiteExecutionListener
com.example.listeners.ScreenshotListener
```

**4. Programmatic Configuration**

```java
import org.testng.TestNG;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public class ProgrammaticListenerConfig {
    
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        TestNG testng = new TestNG();
        
        // Add test classes
        List<String> suites = new ArrayList<>();
        suites.add("testng.xml");
        testng.setTestSuites(suites);
        
        // Add listeners programmatically
        testng.addListener(new TestExecutionListener());
        testng.addListener(new SuiteExecutionListener());
        testng.addListener(new ScreenshotListener());
        
        // Run tests
        testng.run();
    }
}
```

**5. Maven Surefire Configuration**

```xml
<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
            <configuration>
                <properties>
                    <property>
                        <name>listener</name>
                        <value>com.example.listeners.TestExecutionListener,
                               com.example.listeners.SuiteExecutionListener</value>
                    </property>
                </properties>
            </configuration>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>
```

**6. Gradle Configuration**

```groovy
test {
    useTestNG() {
        listeners << 'com.example.listeners.TestExecutionListener'
        listeners << 'com.example.listeners.SuiteExecutionListener'
    }
}
```

**7. System Property**

```bash
java -cp testng.jar:build/classes \
  -Dtestng.listener=com.example.listeners.TestExecutionListener \
  org.testng.TestNG testng.xml
```

**8. Multiple Listeners - Execution Order**

Listeners are executed in the order they are declared:

```xml
<listeners>
    <!-- These run in order: first LoggingListener, then ScreenshotListener, then EmailListener -->
    <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.LoggingListener"/>
    <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ScreenshotListener"/>
    <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.EmailListener"/>
</listeners>
```

**9. Listener Inheritance**

Listeners are inherited by subclasses:

```java
@Listeners(LoggingListener.class)
public class BaseTest {
    // All subclasses inherit the listener
}

public class ChildTest extends BaseTest {
    @Test
    public void testInheritedListener() {
        // LoggingListener will be active
    }
}
```

**10. Disabling Listeners**

```xml
<suite name="Suite with Disabled Listeners">
    <listeners>
        <!-- Include normally -->
        <listener class-name="com.example.listeners.ActiveListener"/>
        
        <!-- Can't directly disable, but you can control via code -->
    </listeners>
</suite>
```

**Comparison of Configuration Methods:**

| Method | Pros | Cons | Best For |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| **testng.xml** | Centralized, flexible, externalized | Requires XML file | Most projects, team environments |
| **@Listeners** | Simple, test-specific | Hard to change without recompile | Small projects, specific tests |
| **Service Loader** | Automatic discovery | Complex setup | Library development |
| **Programmatic** | Full control | Requires code changes | Custom test runners |
| **Maven/Gradle** | Build integration | Tied to build tool | CI/CD environments |
| **System Property** | Quick, dynamic | Limited to one listener | Debugging, temporary needs |

content.title: Leveraging TestNG's Built-in Reporting Capabilities
content.explanation:
**Out-of-the-Box Reporting:**

TestNG comes with several built-in reporters that generate various types of test reports automatically.

**Default Reports Location:**

After running tests, TestNG creates a `test-output` directory with multiple reports:

```
test-output/
├── index.html                 # Main HTML report (default)
├── emailable-report.html      # Email-friendly HTML report
├── testng-results.xml         # Raw results in XML
├── testng-failed.xml          # Failed tests only (for rerun)
├── old/                       # Previous run archives
├── suites/                     # Suite-specific HTML reports
│   ├── SuiteName.html
│   └── SuiteName.xml
├── reports/                    # JUnit-style XML reports
│   └── testsuites.html
└── junitreports/               # JUnit-compatible XML
    └── TEST-com.example.Test.xml
```

**Built-in Reporters:**

| Reporter Class | File Generated | Purpose |
|----------------|----------------|---------|
| **`org.testng.reporters.HTMLReporter`** | `index.html` | Main HTML report with test results, groups, and timelines |
| **`org.testng.reporters.EmailableReporter2`** | `emailable-report.html` | Simplified HTML report suitable for email |
| **`org.testng.reporters.XMLReporter`** | `testng-results.xml` | Detailed XML results for further processing |
| **`org.testng.reporters.JUnitReportReporter`** | `junitreports/*.xml` | JUnit-compatible XML for CI tools |
| **`org.testng.reporters.FailedReporter`** | `testng-failed.xml` | List of failed tests to rerun |
| **`org.testng.reporters.TextReporter`** | Console | Plain text summary to console |
| **`org.testng.reporters.ExitCodeListener`** | Exit code | Returns appropriate exit code for build tools |

**Configuring Built-in Reporters:**

```xml
<suite name="Reporter Demo Suite">
    <listeners>
        <!-- Enable specific reporters with configuration -->
        <listener class-name="org.testng.reporters.HTMLReporter">
            <parameter name="outputDirectory" value="custom-reports/html"/>
            <parameter name="generateGroupsReport" value="true"/>
            <parameter name="generateReporterOutput" value="true"/>
        </listener>
        
        <listener class-name="org.testng.reporters.EmailableReporter2">
            <parameter name="outputDirectory" value="custom-reports/email"/>
            <parameter name="sortBy" value="INSTANCE"/>
        </listener>
        
        <listener class-name="org.testng.reporters.XMLReporter">
            <parameter name="outputDirectory" value="custom-reports/xml"/>
            <parameter name="generateTestResultAttributes" value="true"/>
        </listener>
    </listeners>
    
    <test name="Reporter Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.example.ReporterTest"/>
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>
```

**Programmatic Configuration:**

```java
TestNG testng = new TestNG();
testng.setOutputDirectory("custom-reports");

// Add specific reporters
HTMLReporter htmlReporter = new HTMLReporter();
EmailableReporter2 emailReporter = new EmailableReporter2();
XMLReporter xmlReporter = new XMLReporter();

testng.addListener(htmlReporter);
testng.addListener(emailReporter);
testng.addListener(xmlReporter);
```

**Reading index.html - Main Report Sections:**

1. **Suite Summary**: Overall pass/fail statistics
2. **Test Results**: List of all tests with status
3. **Groups**: Results grouped by test groups
4. **Reporter Output**: Custom log messages
5. **Timeline**: Test execution timeline
6. **Configuration Methods**: Setup/teardown results

**Failed Tests Report (testng-failed.xml):**

```xml

<suite name="Failed suite [Failed Suite]">
    <test name="Failed tests">

    </test>
</suite>
```

**Rerun Failed Tests:**
```bash

```

**JUnit Reports for CI/CD:**

Jenkins, GitLab CI, and other CI tools can consume JUnit XML reports:

```xml

    stages {
        stage('Test') {
            steps {
                sh 'mvn clean test'
            }
        }
    }
    post {
        always {
            junit 'test-output/junitreports/*.xml'
        }
    }
}
```

content.title: Complete GitLab CI Pipeline for TestNG
content.scenario: A comprehensive GitLab CI pipeline for a Java application with TestNG tests.
content.outcome: A fully automated pipeline with test stages, reporting, and quality gates.
content.prevention: Automated testing ensures code quality before deployment.
content.details:
**.gitlab-ci.yml:**

```yaml
# Complete GitLab CI pipeline for TestNG
stages:
  - build
  - unit-test
  - integration-test
  - ui-test
  - report
  - deploy

variables:
  MAVEN_OPTS: "-Dmaven.repo.local=$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.m2/repository"
  MAVEN_CLI_OPTS: "--batch-mode --errors --fail-at-end --show-version"
  TEST_ENV: "staging"
  BROWSER: "chrome"
  HEADLESS: "true"

cache:
  key: "${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}"
  paths:
    - .m2/repository/

before_script:
  - echo "Starting pipeline for branch $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH"
  - java -version
  - mvn -version

# Build job
build:
  stage: build
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS compile
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - target/classes/
    expire_in: 1 hour

# Unit tests (fast, run on all commits)
unit-test:
  stage: unit-test
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS test -Dgroups=unit
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - target/surefire-reports/
    reports:
      junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
    expire_in: 1 week

# Integration tests (run on main branch and MRs)
integration-test:
  stage: integration-test
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS test -Dgroups=integration -Denvironment=$TEST_ENV
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - target/surefire-reports/
    reports:
      junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
  only:
    - main
    - merge_requests

# UI tests with matrix strategy
ui-test:
  stage: ui-test
  parallel:
    matrix:
      - BROWSER: [chrome, firefox]
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS test -Dgroups=ui -Dbrowser=$BROWSER -Dheadless=$HEADLESS
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - target/surefire-reports/
      - target/screenshots/
    reports:
      junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
  only:
    - main
    - schedules

# Performance tests (run on schedule)
performance-test:
  stage: integration-test
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS test -Dgroups=performance
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - target/surefire-reports/
      - target/performance-reports/
  only:
    - schedules
  when: manual  # Manual trigger option

# Quality gate
quality-gate:
  stage: report
  script:
    - |
      echo "Checking test results..."
      
      # Check if test results exist
      if [ ! -f target/surefire-reports/testng-results.xml ]; then
        echo "❌ No test results found"
        exit 1
      fi
      
      # Count critical failures
      CRITICAL_FAILS=$(grep -c 'group="critical".*status="FAIL"' target/surefire-reports/testng-results.xml || true)
      TOTAL_FAILS=$(grep -c 'status="FAIL"' target/surefire-reports/testng-results.xml || true)
      TOTAL_TESTS=$(grep -c '<test-method' target/surefire-reports/testng-results.xml || true)
      
      echo "Critical failures: $CRITICAL_FAILS"
      echo "Total failures: $TOTAL_FAILS"
      echo "Total tests: $TOTAL_TESTS"
      
      # Quality gate rules
      if [ $CRITICAL_FAILS -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "❌ Critical tests failed - blocking deployment"
        exit 1
      fi
      
      if [ $TOTAL_TESTS -gt 0 ]; then
        PASS_RATE=$(( (TOTAL_TESTS - TOTAL_FAILS) * 100 / TOTAL_TESTS ))
        echo "Pass rate: $PASS_RATE%"
        
        if [ $PASS_RATE -lt 95 ]; then
          echo "❌ Pass rate below 95%"
          exit 1
        fi
      fi
      
      echo "✅ Quality gate passed"
  needs:
    - unit-test
    - integration-test
  only:
    - main

# Generate Allure report
allure-report:
  stage: report
  script:
    - mvn allure:report
    - mkdir -p public/allure
    - cp -r target/site/allure-maven-plugin/* public/allure/
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - public/allure/
  only:
    - main

# Deploy to staging
deploy-staging:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - echo "Deploying to staging environment..."
    - ./deploy.sh staging $CI_COMMIT_SHA
  environment:
    name: staging
    url: https://staging.example.com
  only:
    - main
  needs:
    - quality-gate

# Deploy to production (manual approval)
deploy-production:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - echo "Deploying to production..."
    - ./deploy.sh production $CI_COMMIT_SHA
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://example.com
  only:
    - tags
  when: manual
  needs:
    - quality-gate

# Notify on failure
.notify: &notify
  after_script:
    - |
      if [ "$CI_JOB_STATUS" == "failed" ]; then
        curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
          --data "{\"text\":\"❌ Test job ${CI_JOB_NAME} failed in pipeline ${CI_PIPELINE_URL}\"}" \
          $SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
      fi

# Apply notifications to all jobs
unit-test:
  <<: *notify
integration-test:
  <<: *notify
ui-test:
  <<: *notify
```

steps.action: Create `.github/workflows/testng-tests.yml`.
details:
```yaml
name: TestNG Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'  # Run daily at 2 AM
  workflow_dispatch:  # Manual trigger

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        test-type: [unit, integration, ui]
        java-version: [11, 17]
      fail-fast: false  # Don't cancel all if one fails
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v3
        with:
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java-version }}
          distribution: 'temurin'
          cache: maven
      
      - name: Setup Chrome
        uses: browser-actions/setup-chrome@v1
      
      - name: Run ${{ matrix.test-type }} tests
        run: |
          mvn clean test -Dgroups=${{ matrix.test-type }} \
            -Denvironment=${{ secrets.TEST_ENV }} \
            -Dbrowser=chrome \
            -Dheadless=true
      
      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        if: always()  # Upload even if tests fail
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.test-type }}-results-jdk${{ matrix.java-version }}
          path: target/surefire-reports/
      
      - name: Publish Test Report
        uses: mikepenz/action-junit-report@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          report_paths: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
          check_name: ${{ matrix.test-type }} Test Report (JDK ${{ matrix.java-version }})
```

steps.action: Publish reports and send notifications.
details:
```yaml
report:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  needs: [test, matrix-test]
  if: always()
  steps:
    - name: Download all artifacts
      uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
      with:
        path: artifacts/
    
    - name: Merge TestNG reports
      run: |
        # Install TestNG reporter tool
        wget https://github.com/testng-team/testng/releases/download/7.8.0/testng-7.8.0.jar
        
        # Merge all testng-results.xml files
        find artifacts -name "testng-results.xml" -exec echo {} \; > report_files.txt
        java -cp testng-7.8.0.jar org.testng.reporters.XMLReporter report_files.txt merged-results.xml
    
    - name: Generate HTML report
      run: |
        # Generate combined HTML report
        java -cp testng-7.8.0.jar org.testng.reporters.HTMLReporter merged-results.xml merged-report
    
    - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
      uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
      with:

    - name: Send Slack notification
```

```yaml
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: screenshots-${{ matrix.browser }}
          path: target/screenshots/

  # Quality gate
  quality-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [unit-tests, integration-tests, ui-tests]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Download all test results
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: artifacts/
      
      - name: Check quality gates
        run: |
          # Install required tools
          sudo apt-get install -y xmlstarlet
          
          FAILED=0
          
          # Check each test result file
          for file in $(find artifacts -name "testng-results.xml"); do
            echo "Checking $file"
            
            # Check for critical failures
            CRITICAL=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "count(//test-method[@groups='critical'][@status='FAIL'])" $file)
            if [ $CRITICAL -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "❌ Critical failures found in $file"
              FAILED=1
            fi
            
            # Calculate pass rate
            TOTAL=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "count(//test-method)" $file)
            FAILED_TESTS=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "count(//test-method[@status='FAIL'])" $file)
            
            if [ $TOTAL -gt 0 ]; then
              PASS_RATE=$(( (TOTAL - FAILED_TESTS) * 100 / TOTAL ))
              echo "  Pass rate: $PASS_RATE%"
              
              if [ $PASS_RATE -lt 95 ]; then
                echo "❌ Pass rate below 95% in $file"
                FAILED=1
              fi
            fi
          done
          
          exit $FAILED

  # Deploy based on results
  deploy:
    needs: quality-gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: success() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    environment: ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Deploy to ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}
        run: |
          echo "Deploying to ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}..."
          ./deploy.sh ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}

  # Notify on completion
  notify:
    needs: [unit-tests, integration-tests, ui-tests, quality-gate]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Send Slack notification
        uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
        with:
          status: ${{ job.status }}
          fields: repo,message,commit,author,workflow
          text: |
            ${{ job.status == 'success' && '✅' || '❌' }} Test run completed
            Quality Gate: ${{ needs.quality-gate.result }}
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
```
